ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $P$ is a point on $\odot O$. If $\angle PAB=32^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle PBA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, \\
$\therefore \angle APB=90^\circ$ \\
Since $\angle PAB=32^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle PBA=\boxed{58^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, \\ $\therefore \angle APB=90^\circ$ \\ Since $\angle PAB=32^\circ$, \\ $\therefore \angle PBA=\boxed{58^\circ}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle, with the center marked as O; the horizontal line segment AB passes through the center O, and endpoints A and B are on the circle, so AB is the diameter of the circle. Point P is located on the upper arc of the circle; PA and PB are connected, forming triangle APB. Reasoning: It is known that ∠PAB = 32°. Because AB is the diameter of the circle and P is on the circle, according to Thales' theorem, the inscribed angle subtended by the diameter, ∠APB = 90°. In triangle APB, the sum of the three interior angles is 180°, so ∠PBA = 180° - 90° - 32° = 58°.
